Campaigns buy geography by the slice they think in: a city's codes for an event, a state's for a launch. The list in hand ends the guessing.

Chicago's city ZIPs cluster in the 606xx range; Cook County adds the suburban 600xx–608xx ring that is not Chicago at all. Overlapping but different lists — choosing the wrong slice mails the suburbs and calls it the city.

Some ZIP areas cross county and even city lines — a delivery route does not stop for a surveyor. Such codes appear on both counties' lists, because the postal geography and the civic geography were never the same map.

popular_table.note: The standing ZIP caveat applies: ZIP codes are USPS delivery constructs, and list membership follows the best public ZIP-to-place data — the USPS itself is the authority for delivery questions.

faq: Why is a ZIP on two counties' lists?
Its delivery area crosses the line. Postal routes were drawn for mail, not for census neatness — dual membership is the honest representation, not a bug.
USPS assigns each ZIP a preferred city name that can differ from the municipality the address sits in. The city slice follows postal naming and says so; civic truth lives with the boundary tools.
Codes serving one facility exist in the postal file; list tools vary in carrying them. For mailing work their absence rarely matters; for completeness claims, the note on the list governs.
How often do ZIP lists change?
USPS creates, splits and retires codes continuously as delivery grows. Any frozen list is a snapshot — for production mail, current CASS-grade data is the standard.
Can I get the list as a file?
The results copy out as text for your documents and spreadsheets — the working form of a reference list — with the map view one click away in the ZIP Code Map.
Different systems, different tools: Canada's FSAs and UK postcode districts live in the Location family's postcode tools, sliced their own ways.
The +4 refines delivery within a ZIP and multiplies the list a thousandfold — reference lists live at the 5-digit level, where geography still means something.
